what_happened: The design job "Design removing the local landing branch from landing" was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier raised three major findings and no blockers. (1) The measurement method in section 6 of docs/design/per-job-pr-landing.md cannot score the 5.0-minute prediction, because it ignores the measurement effect that the repository's own notes document. (2) Sections 1 and 4 explain the 1996.9-minute landing figure as a real serial queue wait. That contradicts the design notes the request cites and the note's own 5.0 prediction. (3) There is no CHANGELOG.md entry, although it is an expected deliverable and the changelog default applies. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that checks a note's headline numbers against the recorded data and the notes it cites before the note builds on them. The landing-wait figure was taken at face value, though the cited notes say it is mostly a measurement effect. The same wrong premise was rejected one job earlier (20261109-014709-kxrd), and the follow-up job did not carry that finding forward. The changelog default is also left to the producer's memory, and nothing compares the diff with the expected deliverables. Criteria check that sections exist, not that the premise or the measurement method is sound. Only the verifier, at the end, reads the evidence.
prevention: Add a required premise-check step for design jobs. Before drafting, the producer lists each headline number in the request and states its source: a record query, or the cited note. It also states whether that source flags the number as an artifact. The note must carry that table in its problem section, and a code check must confirm the table exists. Any measurement plan must name how it separates real waiting from measurement effect. For follow-ups of a rejected design job, the reading must copy forward each prior verifier finding as a criterion. A code check must compare the diff's file list with the expected deliverables, including CHANGELOG.md, before the verifier runs. Together these would have stopped this class: a wrong premise, a method that cannot score the claim, and a missing changelog.
proposed_request:
Design: remove the local landing branch from landing (per-job PR landing), in docs/design/per-job-pr-landing.md. Revise the note after the earlier rejection. Outcome: the note must state a landing-time prediction that can be scored against real data.
Acceptance:
- Section 1 (problem) has a table of every headline number. Each row gives its source: a record query or the cited note, e.g. agent-and-build-slots.md §6.1. Each row says whether that source calls the number a measurement effect. The 1996.9-minute landing figure is described as mostly a measurement effect, not a real serial queue wait, and sections 1 and 4 agree with the 5.0-minute prediction.
- Section 6 gives a measurement method that separates real waiting from the measurement effect. It names which timestamps it uses. It says how the 5.0-minute prediction will be scored on jobs after landing.
- Each finding from the earlier rejections of this design (job 20261109-014709-kxrd and this one) is fixed, or the note says why it does not apply.
- The note surveys the existing landing code and states what already exists before proposing changes.
- CHANGELOG.md has an entry for this note, as the changelog default requires.
- Only the design note and CHANGELOG.md change.
